caseMeta.title: Hip Fracture - Hospital Day 1
learningObjectives: Perform neurovascular checks and pain reassessment for a patient with a hip fracture.
Prioritize pre-operative care for an older adult with a hip fracture: pain control, neurovascular checks, NPO, VTE and bleeding-risk management.
Implement post-operative hip fracture care: weight bearing, hip precautions, early mobilization, incentive spirometry, Foley removal and pressure-injury prevention.
Recognize and prevent delirium, post-operative anemia, constipation, urinary retention and VTE in an older adult.
Coordinate PT/OT and case management for discharge to rehab.
Connect assessment findings, labs and orders to prioritize nursing care.

problems.name: Hip fracture (intertrochanteric)
problems.details: Right hip fracture after a fall; awaiting intramedullary nail fixation within 24-48 hours.

problems.name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
problems.details: Chronic diabetes on basal insulin and oral therapy at home.

problems.name: Hypertension
problems.details: Chronic hypertension on home antihypertensive therapy.

problems.name: Coronary artery disease
problems.details: Known atherosclerotic coronary disease on aspirin, statin and beta blocker.

problems.name: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
problems.details: Chronic HFrEF (EF about 35%) on beta blocker and loop diuretic.

problems.name: Atrial fibrillation
problems.details: Chronic atrial fibrillation on rate control and anticoagulation.

problems.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
problems.details: Chronic obstructive lung disease; baseline SpO2 about 90-92%.

problems.name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
problems.details: Chronic GERD on a proton pump inhibitor.

problems.name: Depression / anxiety
problems.details: Chronic depression and anxiety on an SSRI.

problems.name: Chronic constipation
problems.details: Functional constipation managed with daily osmotic and stimulant laxatives.

problems.name: Peripheral neuropathy
problems.details: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy of both feet.

problems.name: History of MRSA infection / colonization
problems.details: Prior MRSA skin abscess; nares colonized on screening.

problems.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
problems.details: Seropositive RA on methotrexate 15 mg once weekly, folic acid, hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisone.

problems.name: Chronic peripheral edema
problems.details: Chronic bilateral dependent leg edema with fragile skin.

problems.name: Frailty
problems.details: Frail older adult with weight loss, weakness and reduced reserve; high risk of delirium and functional decline.

orders.name: 2 g sodium, consistent carbohydrate diet
orders.instructions: Heart-healthy; encourage fluids and protein. Offer snacks; set up meals (patient flat in bed). Modified for 2 g sodium, consistent carbohydrate.

orders.name: Bed rest, non-weight bearing right leg
orders.instructions: Keep right leg in neutral rotation, pillow between knees, heels off the bed. Log roll with 2 staff. Bedpan or assisted bedside commode only.

orders.name: Buck's skin traction (5 lb), comfort until surgery
orders.instructions: Apply foam boot with 5 lb weight to right leg for comfort; weights hang free. Check skin of heel, malleoli and fibular head every shift. Remove for surgery.
nursingConsiderations: Assess for peroneal nerve pressure (foot drop, numbness over top of foot).
Check that traction ropes are free and weights are not resting on the floor or bed.

orders.name: Neurovascular checks right leg
orders.instructions: Check color, warmth, capillary refill, dorsalis pedis/posterior tibial pulses, sensation and ability to move toes. Notify surgeon for pallor, coolness, loss of pulse, numbness, or severe pain unrelieved by medication.
nursingConsiderations: Post-op: report increasing thigh swelling or tightness (hematoma / compartment syndrome).

orders.name: Anticoagulant and antiplatelet review (pre-operative)
orders.instructions: Confirm and document date and time of last dose of any anticoagulant (apixaban, rivaroxaban, warfarin) or antiplatelet (clopidogrel, aspirin). Hold anticoagulants. Notify surgeon and anesthesia (spinal/epidural timing). INR checked.
nursingConsiderations: Aspirin 81 mg may be continued if ordered; do not give clopidogrel, apixaban or warfarin until the surgeon clears it.

orders.name: Type and screen
orders.instructions: Blood bank specimen; armband required. Keep sample valid (repeat every 72 hours).

orders.name: Transfusion threshold: Hgb below 8 g/dL or symptomatic
orders.instructions: Restrictive transfusion strategy: transfuse 1 unit PRBC for Hgb below 8 g/dL, or for chest pain, symptomatic tachycardia or hypotension. Recheck Hgb after each unit.
nursingConsiderations: Notify provider for Hgb below 8, HR above 110, SBP below 90, new dyspnea, dizziness or pallor.

orders.name: Delirium prevention bundle
orders.instructions: Reorient often; glasses, hearing aids and dentures within reach; day-night routine and lights off at night; treat pain; avoid benzodiazepines and anticholinergics; early mobilization; hydration; avoid restraints. Screen with CAM every shift.
nursingConsiderations: New confusion: check pain, urinary retention, constipation, hypoxia, infection, glucose and recent medications before giving any sedative.

orders.name: Pressure injury prevention
orders.instructions: Braden each shift; reposition every 2 hours (30-degree tilt on the non-operative side or per surgeon); float heels with pillows/boots; pressure-redistribution mattress; keep skin dry; assess sacrum, heels and hips.
nursingConsiderations: Older adults lying on a hard floor or ED stretcher are at high risk for sacral and heel injury.

orders.name: Incentive spirometry
orders.instructions: Teach and encourage deep breaths with sustained inspiration; record achieved volume.
nursingConsiderations: Goal volume documented by RT/nursing; report below 50% of goal.

orders.name: Pre-operative checklist, consent and site verification
orders.instructions: Verify consent (or health care proxy if lacking capacity), ID and allergy bands, right hip marked, NPO status, hearing aids/dentures plan, last void, antibiotic within 60 minutes before incision, skin traction off.

orders.name: Sequential compression devices
orders.instructions: Apply to both legs (or non-operative leg only if the operative leg is swollen) until fully ambulatory.

orders.name: Case management consult: post-acute rehab planning
orders.instructions: Evaluate for skilled nursing facility / inpatient rehab. Medicare 3-midnight qualifying stay; start insurance authorization early.

orders.name: Point-of-care blood glucose
orders.instructions: Check before meals and at bedtime; every 6 hours while NPO. Treat per hypoglycemia protocol.

orders.name: Hypoglycemia protocol
orders.instructions: Follow facility hypoglycemia protocol: 15 g fast carbohydrate if awake, recheck in 15 minutes; dextrose 50% IV if NPO or unable to swallow.

orders.name: Daily weight
orders.instructions: Same scale each morning before breakfast; report gain of more than 2 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week.

orders.name: Supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula
orders.instructions: Start 1-2 L/min; titrate to SpO2 88-92%. Do not exceed target (CO2 retention risk).
nursingConsiderations: Goal SpO2 is 88-92%, NOT higher; notify provider for drowsiness or SpO2 below 88%.

orders.name: Respiratory therapy evaluate and treat
orders.instructions: RT to assess, administer nebulizers, and review inhaler technique.

orders.name: Bowel movement record; notify provider if no BM in 48-72 hours
orders.instructions: Record date, amount and consistency (Bristol scale). Encourage fluids, fiber and walking as tolerated; use the toilet at the same time each day. Rule out impaction before giving more laxatives.

orders.name: Foot and skin inspection; protect numb feet
orders.instructions: Check both feet for pressure areas, blisters, wounds. Test water temperature with the elbow; no heating pads on feet; shoes or non-skid socks for all walking.

orders.name: Contact precautions
orders.instructions: Gown and gloves for all contact; dedicated stethoscope/equipment; private room; hand hygiene with soap and water or alcohol rub.

orders.name: Chlorhexidine bathing
orders.instructions: Daily bath with 2% chlorhexidine cloths from neck down (avoid face, eyes, mucous membranes) to reduce MRSA burden.

orders.name: Chronic steroid precautions
orders.instructions: Long-term corticosteroid user: never skip doses; provider to consider stress-dose steroids (hydrocortisone) for hypotension, sepsis or surgery. Check glucose with meals while hyperglycemic; watch for infection (fever may be blunted), GI upset and mood change.
nursingConsiderations: Hypotension unresponsive to fluids in a steroid-dependent patient may be adrenal insufficiency: notify the provider.

orders.name: Immunosuppression / infection precautions
orders.instructions: Immunosuppressed (methotrexate + prednisone): strict hand hygiene, no sick visitors, no live vaccines, monitor closely for infection. Fever and WBC response may be blunted: report temperature 100.4 F or higher, new cough, dysuria, wound drainage or confusion.
nursingConsiderations: Infection can progress quickly in immunosuppressed patients; escalate early.

orders.name: Avoid NSAIDs (ibuprofen, ketorolac, naproxen)
orders.instructions: No NSAIDs: CKD, anticoagulant or a cardiac/renal/bleeding condition. Use acetaminophen, topical lidocaine, heat or ice instead. Question any NSAID order and notify the provider.
nursingConsiderations: NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with anticoagulants and can cause acute kidney injury in CKD.

orders.name: Elevate legs and protect edematous skin
orders.instructions: Elevate legs on pillows above heart level when in bed/chair; no tight socks; inspect legs and heels each shift for blisters, weeping, skin tears or redness; pad bony areas; avoid adhesive on legs. Compression stockings only if pulses present, no decompensated HF.

orders.name: Skin assessment with Braden Score every shift
orders.instructions: Check heels, sacrum and edematous areas.

orders.name: Frailty precautions: falls, delirium and skin tears
orders.instructions: High fall risk (bed alarm, assist x1-2, scheduled toileting); delirium prevention (glasses/hearing aids, orientation, sleep, avoid sedatives); fragile skin: paper tape or silicone dressings, pad bony areas, no friction when repositioning.

orders.name: Dietitian consult and nutrition support
orders.instructions: Weight loss and low albumin: high-protein supplements between meals, feeding assistance, weekly weights.

orders.name: PT/OT evaluation and early mobilization
orders.instructions: Up to chair for meals, ambulate with assistance 3 times daily; evaluate for rehab placement.

orders.name: Goals of care and polypharmacy review
orders.instructions: Palliative/geriatrics input as needed; review code status and deprescribe where possible. Start low and go slow with new medications.

orders.name: Pacemaker precautions
orders.instructions: Programmed lower rate 60 bpm: notify provider for pulse below 60 or symptoms of failure to capture/sense (dizziness, syncope, fatigue). No MRI unless the system is MRI-conditional and cleared; electrocautery needs a device plan.

orders.name: No BP, blood draws, IV access or injections in right arm (mastectomy)
orders.instructions: Protect the right arm from lymphedema and infection: no BP cuff, venipuncture, IV or injections. Use the left arm. Report swelling, redness or heaviness.

orders.name: Tobacco cessation counseling
orders.instructions: Offer cessation counseling and quitline information before discharge.

orders.name: Vital signs
orders.instructions: Notify provider for SBP below 90 or above 180, HR above 120 or below 50, RR above 28, SpO2 below 90%, or temperature above 101.5 F.

orders.name: Strict intake and output
orders.instructions: Record all oral and IV intake and all output (urine, drains, emesis).

orders.name: Fall precautions
orders.instructions: Call light in reach, bed low, non-skid footwear, assist with ambulation.

orders.name: CBC and basic metabolic panel
orders.instructions: Draw at 0500.

orders.name: X-ray right hip and pelvis (AP pelvis, AP and cross-table lateral right hip)
orders.instructions: Perform X-ray right hip and pelvis (AP pelvis, AP and cross-table lateral right hip).
orders.rationale: Right hip pain and shortened, externally rotated leg after a fall

orders.name: Chest x-ray, portable
orders.instructions: Perform Chest x-ray, portable.

orders.name: 12-lead ECG
orders.instructions: Perform 12-lead ECG.
orders.rationale: Pre-operative evaluation (syncope excluded as cause of fall)

orders.name: Consult: Orthopedic Surgery
orders.instructions: Right hip fracture

orders.name: Consult: Hospital Medicine (pre-operative co-management)
orders.instructions: Medical optimization before hip surgery

orders.name: Right cephalomedullary nail fixation of intertrochanteric fracture
orders.instructions: Right cephalomedullary nail fixation of intertrochanteric fracture. Consent, NPO status and pre-op checklist before transport.
nursingConsiderations: Confirm consent is signed and in chart.
Confirm NPO status and last intake time.
Complete pre-op checklist; verify allergy band and site marking.

orders.name: insulin lispro (HUMALOG) correction scale
orders.instructions: Administer Low-dose correction scale Subcutaneous ACHS (before meals and at bedtime).

medication.importantInfo: Give per correction scale only with a meal (or q6h if NPO). Check glucose first and document it. Watch for hypoglycemia.

orders.name: prednisone tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 7.5 mg Oral Daily. Do not hold without a provider order; call the provider if the patient is NPO or vomiting.
nursingConsiderations: Do not hold without a provider order; call the provider if the patient is NPO or vomiting.

medication.importantInfo: Give with food in the morning. Do NOT stop abruptly (adrenal suppression). If NPO or not absorbing, notify the provider for an IV steroid equivalent. Raises glucose and BP, masks fever and infection.
medication.hold: Do not hold without a provider order; call the provider if the patient is NPO or vomiting.

orders.name: senna-docusate (SENOKOT-S) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 2 tablets Oral BID.

medication.importantInfo: Hold for loose stools. Goal: a bowel movement at least every other day; immobility and opioids cause constipation.

orders.name: lisinopril (PRINIVIL,ZESTRIL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 20 mg Oral Daily. Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.

medication.importantInfo: Check BP before giving. Monitor potassium and creatinine. Watch for cough and angioedema.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.

orders.name: aspirin chewable tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 81 mg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor for bleeding. Continue through surgery unless surgeon directs otherwise.

orders.name: metoprolol tartrate (LOPRESSOR) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 25 mg Oral BID. Hold and notify provider if HR below 55 or SBP below 100.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider if HR below 55 or SBP below 100.

medication.importantInfo: Check BP and apical HR before giving. May give with a sip of water while NPO unless told otherwise.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider if HR below 55 or SBP below 100.

orders.name: carvedilol (COREG) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 6.25 mg Oral BID. Hold and notify provider if HR below 55 or SBP below 100.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider if HR below 55 or SBP below 100.

medication.importantInfo: Give with food. Check BP and HR before giving.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider if HR below 55 or SBP below 100.

orders.name: furosemide (LASIX) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor BP, urine output, potassium, creatinine and weight.

orders.name: fluticasone-salmeterol (ADVAIR DISKUS) inhaler
orders.instructions: Administer 250/50 mcg, 1 inhalation Inhaled BID.

medication.importantInfo: Rinse mouth after use. Check inhaler technique.

orders.name: pantoprazole (PROTONIX) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Give 30-60 minutes before breakfast.

orders.name: sertraline (ZOLOFT) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 50 mg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Do not stop abruptly. Monitor mood and bleeding risk with other anticoagulants.

orders.name: polyethylene glycol (MIRALAX) powder
orders.instructions: Administer 17 g in 8 oz fluid Oral Daily. Hold for loose stools; notify provider if no BM in 3 days.
nursingConsiderations: Hold for loose stools; notify provider if no BM in 3 days.

medication.importantInfo: Hold for loose stools. Dissolve in 4-8 oz of liquid. Goal: soft BM every 1-2 days.
medication.hold: Hold for loose stools; notify provider if no BM in 3 days.

orders.name: gabapentin (NEURONTIN) capsule
orders.instructions: Administer 300 mg Oral TID.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor sedation and dizziness, especially with opioids. Do not stop abruptly. Dose is adjusted for kidney function.

orders.name: mupirocin (BACTROBAN) 2% nasal ointment
orders.instructions: Administer Apply to each nostril Nasal BID.

medication.importantInfo: Use for 5 days; press nostrils together after application.

orders.name: folic acid tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1 mg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Reduces methotrexate side effects (mouth sores, nausea, cytopenias).

orders.name: hydroxychloroquine (PLAQUENIL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 200 mg Oral BID.

medication.importantInfo: Give with food. Can prolong the QT interval: review ECG/QTc and other QT drugs (ondansetron, azithromycin, fluoroquinolones). Annual eye exam at home.

orders.name: fragrance-free emollient (EUCERIN) lotion
orders.instructions: Administer Thin layer to both legs Topical BID.

medication.importantInfo: Keep stretched edematous skin supple to prevent cracks and weeping.

orders.name: anastrozole (ARIMIDEX) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1 mg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Adjuvant breast cancer therapy. Causes joint aches and bone loss; do not stop without oncology.

orders.name: nicotine (NICODERM CQ) 24 hour patch
orders.instructions: Administer 21 mg Transdermal Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Rotate sites; remove old patch. Do not smoke while wearing patch.

orders.name: ipratropium-albuterol (DUONEB) nebulizer solution
orders.instructions: Administer 3 mL Nebulized Every 6 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Given by RT. Assess breath sounds, HR and work of breathing before and after.

orders.name: acetaminophen (TYLENOL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1,000 mg Oral Every 8 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Scheduled (not PRN) base of multimodal analgesia; opioid-sparing. Maximum 3 g per 24 hours from all sources.

orders.name: heparin injection
orders.instructions: Administer 5,000 units Subcutaneous Every 8 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor for bleeding, bruising, platelets and renal function. Never give if platelets below 50 or active bleeding.

orders.name: cefazolin (ANCEF) IVPB
orders.instructions: Administer 2 g IV Every 8 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Surgical prophylaxis: first dose within 60 minutes before incision, then every 8 hours for no more than 24 hours. Low cross-reactivity with penicillin; verify reaction history. Infuse over 30 minutes.

orders.name: melatonin tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 3 mg Oral Nightly at bedtime.

medication.importantInfo: Delirium-prevention sleep aid. Avoid benzodiazepines, diphenhydramine and zolpidem in older adults.

orders.name: ferrous sulfate tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 325 mg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Give with food if upset stomach. Dark stools are expected. Can worsen constipation. Give 2 hours apart from calcium.

orders.name: cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1,000 units Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Low 25-OH vitamin D with fragility fracture; part of osteoporosis treatment.

orders.name: calcium carbonate (TUMS) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 500 mg Oral BID.

medication.importantInfo: Give with meals. Separate from iron by 2 hours. May worsen constipation.

orders.name: insulin glargine (LANTUS) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 20 units Subcutaneous Nightly at bedtime. Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.
orders.rationale: Type 2 diabetes (home basal insulin, reduced 20% while NPO)
nursingConsiderations: Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.

medication.importantInfo: Basal insulin. Give even when NPO (dose reduced). Check glucose first; hold and call provider if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.
medication.hold: Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.

orders.name: atorvastatin (LIPITOR) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Oral Nightly at bedtime.

medication.importantInfo: Report unexplained muscle pain or weakness.

orders.name: apixaban (ELIQUIS) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 5 mg Oral BID.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor for bleeding. HIGH-ALERT: do not give if the patient is scheduled for or just had surgery until the surgeon clears it.

orders.name: methotrexate (TREXALL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 15 mg Oral Once weekly. HOLD and notify provider for fever or infection, WBC below 3.0, platelets below 100, rising creatinine, mouth sores, new cough or dyspnea. Never give daily.
nursingConsiderations: HOLD and notify provider for fever or infection, WBC below 3.0, platelets below 100, rising creatinine, mouth sores, new cough or dyspnea. Never give daily.

medication.importantInfo: WEEKLY drug: ONE dose on ONE day each week. Daily dosing has caused fatal toxicity (bone marrow, mucositis, liver). Verify the dose day and last dose with pharmacy and the patient before giving. Check CBC, creatinine and ALT.
medication.hold: HOLD and notify provider for fever or infection, WBC below 3.0, platelets below 100, rising creatinine, mouth sores, new cough or dyspnea. Never give daily.

orders.name: enoxaparin (LOVENOX) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Subcutaneous Daily. Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor for bleeding, bruising, platelets and renal function. Never give if platelets below 50 or active bleeding.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.

orders.name: lactated Ringer's infusion
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mL/hr IV Continuous at 40 mL/hr.
nursingConsiderations: Reduced rate for heart failure/ESRD; assess lungs, edema and weight daily.

medication.importantInfo: Assess lungs, edema, I&O and daily weight. Check IV site each shift.

orders.name: morphine injection
orders.instructions: Administer 2 mg IV Every 3 hours PRN severe pain (7-10). Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.
nursingConsiderations: Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.

medication.importantInfo: HIGH-ALERT. Low starting dose for an older adult. Assess pain, sedation (RASS), RR and SpO2 before and 15-30 minutes after. Hold for RR below 10 or oversedation. Watch for new confusion.
medication.hold: Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.

orders.name: oxycodone (ROXICODONE) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 5 mg Oral Every 4 hours PRN moderate pain (4-6). Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.
nursingConsiderations: Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.

medication.importantInfo: HIGH-ALERT. Low dose for age. Assess pain and sedation before and 30-60 minutes after. Hold for RR below 10 or oversedation. Give with a bowel regimen. Opioids are a leading cause of post-operative delirium and falls.
medication.hold: Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.

orders.name: ondansetron (ZOFRAN) injection
orders.frequency: Every 8 hours PRN nausea or vomiting
orders.instructions: Administer 4 mg IV Every 8 hours PRN nausea or vomiting.

medication.importantInfo: Check QTc before repeated dosing in an older adult. Reassess nausea in 30 minutes. Preferred over promethazine (anticholinergic, delirium risk).

orders.name: polyethylene glycol (MIRALAX) powder
orders.frequency: Once daily PRN no bowel movement in 24 hours
orders.instructions: Administer 17 g Oral Once daily PRN no bowel movement in 24 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Mix in 4-8 oz of fluid. Hold for loose stools. Goal: bowel movement by post-op day 3.

orders.name: albuterol (PROVENTIL) nebulizer solution
orders.frequency: Every 2 hours PRN wheezing or shortness of breath
orders.instructions: Administer 2.5 mg Nebulized Every 2 hours PRN wheezing or shortness of breath.

medication.importantInfo: Check HR before and after; may cause tremor and tachycardia.

orders.name: bisacodyl (DULCOLAX) suppository
orders.frequency: Once daily PRN no bowel movement in 48 hours
orders.instructions: Administer 10 mg Rectal Once daily PRN no bowel movement in 48 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Do not use with suspected obstruction, ileus or rectal bleeding. Give 15-60 minutes before the expected BM.

orders.name: lactated Ringer's bolus
orders.instructions: Administer 250 mL IV Once.
orders.rationale: Dehydration after prolonged lying / poor intake before the fall
nursingConsiderations: Stop the bolus and notify provider for new crackles, dyspnea or SpO2 drop.
Reduced bolus volume for heart failure/ESRD; reassess after each 250-500 mL.

medication.importantInfo: Reassess vital signs, lung sounds and urine output after the bolus.

stickyNotes.title: Pre-op
stickyNotes.body: NPO after midnight (sips with essential meds). OR about 0800. Verify consent, last dose of blood thinners, right hip marking.

stickyNotes.title: Fall / delirium risk
stickyNotes.body: High fall risk: bed alarm, assist x2 early on, never leave on commode. Screen for delirium every shift; avoid sedatives.

stickyNotes.title: Anticoagulant / antiplatelet
stickyNotes.body: Verify last dose of any home blood thinner before surgery. Enoxaparin plus SCDs for VTE prevention; hold doses per anesthesia timing after spinal.

stickyNotes.title: MRSA history
stickyNotes.body: Prior MRSA. Contact precautions. For new skin, bone, line, pneumonia or sepsis concerns the empiric regimen should include MRSA coverage (vancomycin or linezolid) until cultures result.

stickyNotes.title: Restricted arm
stickyNotes.body: Right arm: no BP, IV, venipuncture or injections.

notes.title: Hospitalist Medical Co-management Consult
notes.author: S. Patel, MD
notes.summary: Medical co-management of chronic conditions peri-operatively.
notes.body:
**Reason for consult**
- Medical co-management of chronic conditions during admission for hip fracture (intertrochanteric).

**Assessment and plan**
**Type 2 diabetes mellitus**
- Basal glargine with ACHS correction lispro; goal glucose 140-180 mg/dL.
- Metformin held while inpatient.
- Hypoglycemia protocol in place.

**Hypertension**
- Continue home antihypertensive; BP goal below 140/90.

**Coronary artery disease**
- Continue aspirin, statin and beta blocker; telemetry not required unless chest pain; call for chest pain or ECG changes.

**Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction**
- Euvolemic to mildly dry on exam; continue beta blocker; judicious IV fluids with daily weights.
- Continue home diuretic.

**Atrial fibrillation**
- Rate controlled on metoprolol/carvedilol.
- Apixaban held peri-operatively; resume per surgery (typically 24-48 h post-op) with DVT prophylaxis meanwhile.

**Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease**
- Scheduled DuoNebs q6h with PRN albuterol; maintenance inhaler continued.
- Oxygen goal SpO2 88-92%; avoid over-oxygenation.
- Tobacco cessation counseling and nicotine replacement.

**Chronic anemia**
- Baseline Hgb about 10; transfuse only for Hgb below 7 (or symptomatic); trend CBC.

**Gastroesophageal reflux disease**
- Continue pantoprazole (IV while NPO).

**Depression / anxiety**
- Continue sertraline; screen for suicidal ideation per policy.

**Chronic constipation**
- Continue daily regimen (hold for loose stools); opioids and immobility make it worse: add or increase laxatives early.
- Check for fecal impaction if no BM in 3 days or overflow diarrhea.

**Peripheral neuropathy**
- Continue neuropathic agent (renally dose); sedation risk if combined with opioids.
- Foot checks every shift; falls precautions.

**History of MRSA infection / colonization**
- Contact precautions; decolonization protocol (mupirocin x5 days, chlorhexidine baths).
- Include MRSA coverage in empiric antibiotics for new infection; trough/AUC monitoring if vancomycin is used.

**Rheumatoid arthritis**
- Methotrexate (WEEKLY) held during acute illness; resume only when the provider confirms infection/AKI resolved.
- Continue folic acid, hydroxychloroquine and prednisone (do not stop steroid abruptly; stress-dose if septic/hypotensive).
- Immunosuppression precautions; monitor CBC and creatinine.
- Avoid NSAIDs if CKD or anticoagulated.

**Chronic peripheral edema**
- Elevation and skin care every shift; daily weight.
- Report weeping, blisters, redness or sudden one-sided swelling (DVT/cellulitis).

**Frailty**
- Early mobility, nutrition support, delirium and fall precautions.
- Start low, go slow with medications; goals-of-care discussion.

**Peri-operative risk**
- Intermediate cardiopulmonary risk; proceed with surgery as planned. Optimize glucose, continue beta blocker, hold anticoagulant and nephrotoxins.

notes.title: General Surgery H&P / Consult
notes.author: R. Alvarez, MD
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
- Right hip pain after a fall; unable to bear weight

**History of present illness**
67-year-old female who tripped on the way to the bathroom at night and fell onto the right side from standing height. Immediate severe right hip and groin pain with inability to stand or bear weight; the right leg was shortened and turned outward when EMS arrived. No loss of consciousness, head strike, chest pain, palpitations or preceding dizziness. Denies numbness or tingling in the foot. Received fentanyl 25 mcg IV from EMS.

**Past medical history**
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus (A1c 8.0%); Hypertension; Coronary artery disease; Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF about 35%); Atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc elevated, on apixaban); COPD; Chronic anemia; GERD; Depression and anxiety; Chronic constipation; Peripheral neuropathy; MRSA infection (prior abscess), colonized; Rheumatoid arthritis (on methotrexate weekly, hydroxychloroquine, prednisone); Chronic bilateral lower extremity edema; Frailty (weight loss, weakness)

**Past surgical history**
- Cholecystectomy (2018); CABG (2022); Coronary stent / PCI (2018); Pacemaker / ICD (2018); Total hip replacement (1989); Mastectomy - right (with axillary node surgery) (2018)

**Home medications**
- insulin glargine (LANTUS) 20 units Subcutaneous Nightly at bedtime
- insulin lispro (HUMALOG) correction scale Low-dose correction scale Subcutaneous ACHS (before meals and at bedtime)
- lisinopril (PRINIVIL,ZESTRIL) 20 mg Oral Daily
- aspirin chewable 81 mg Oral Daily
- atorvastatin (LIPITOR) 40 mg Oral Nightly at bedtime
- metoprolol tartrate (LOPRESSOR) 25 mg Oral BID
- carvedilol (COREG) 6.25 mg Oral BID
- furosemide (LASIX) 40 mg Oral Daily
- apixaban (ELIQUIS) 5 mg Oral BID
- ipratropium-albuterol (DUONEB) nebulizer solution 3 mL Nebulized Every 6 hours
- albuterol (PROVENTIL) nebulizer solution 2.5 mg Nebulized Every 4 hours
- fluticasone-salmeterol (ADVAIR DISKUS) inhaler 250/50 mcg, 1 inhalation Inhaled BID
- ferrous sulfate 325 mg Oral Daily
- pantoprazole (PROTONIX) 40 mg Oral Daily
- sertraline (ZOLOFT) 50 mg Oral Daily
- polyethylene glycol (MIRALAX) powder 17 g in 8 oz fluid Oral Daily
- senna-docusate (SENOKOT-S) 2 tablets Oral BID
- bisacodyl (DULCOLAX) suppository 10 mg Rectal Daily
- gabapentin (NEURONTIN) 300 mg Oral TID
- methotrexate (TREXALL) 15 mg Oral Once weekly
- folic acid 1 mg Oral Daily
- hydroxychloroquine (PLAQUENIL) 200 mg Oral BID
- prednisone 7.5 mg Oral Daily
- fragrance-free emollient (EUCERIN) lotion Thin layer to both legs Topical BID
- anastrozole (ARIMIDEX) 1 mg Oral Daily
- (Metformin held while hospitalized (contrast, acute illness, renal risk).)
- (Home tiotropium replaced by scheduled DuoNebs (avoid duplicate anticholinergic).)
- (Methotrexate 15 mg is taken ONCE WEEKLY (Friday); the chart shows the next dose (10/09/26) and it is NOT a daily drug. Hold during acute infection, AKI or cytopenias until the provider reviews.)

**Allergies**
- Penicillin (Hives); Sulfa drugs (Rash)

**Family history**
- Mother with hypertension and type 2 diabetes; father with coronary artery disease. Mother had a hip fracture in her 80s. No known family history of bleeding disorders.

**Social history**
- Lives with spouse/partner; independent with ADLs and ambulation at baseline; tobacco: current <1 ppd; alcohol: social; other substances: past substance use.

**Review of systems**
- Positive for hip/groin pain and inability to walk. Negative for head injury, neck pain, chest pain, dyspnea, abdominal pain, focal weakness, numbness, fever, or urinary symptoms.

**Vitals**
- T 98.3 F, HR 99, BP 150/89, RR 19, SpO2 91% on room air, pain 6/10 | Wt 70 kg, BMI 26.3

**Physical exam**
- General: Awake and alert, uncomfortable-appearing.
- Cardiovascular: Atrial fibrillation, rate controlled, irregularly irregular; S1 S2 irregularly irregular, no murmur. Edema: Trace bilateral lower extremity edema.
- Respiratory: Diminished bilaterally with scattered end-expiratory wheeze; mildly prolonged expiratory phase.
- Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended. Bowel sounds: active in all four quadrants.
- Neurologic: Alert and oriented x4.
- Skin: Warm, dry; ecchymosis over right lateral hip; no open wounds or skin tears.

**Data**
- Labs: Hemoglobin 8.9 (L); WBC 11.8 (H); Platelets 225; Sodium 137; Potassium 4.2; Creatinine 0.94; INR 1.0; Glucose 201 (H)
- X-ray right hip and pelvis (AP pelvis, AP and cross-table lateral right hip): Unstable right intertrochanteric femur fracture.
- Chest x-ray, portable: No acute cardiopulmonary process.
- 12-lead ECG: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response (rate 84). No acute ST-T wave changes. QTc 436 ms.

**Assessment and plan**
67-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, coronary artery disease, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chronic anemia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, depression / anxiety, chronic constipation, peripheral neuropathy, history of mrsa infection / colonization, rheumatoid arthritis, chronic peripheral edema, frailty admitted with hip fracture (intertrochanteric).

**Hip fracture (intertrochanteric)**
- Intertrochanteric fracture, hemodynamically stable. Medically optimized for surgery; ECG and chest x-ray without acute findings.
- Fascia iliaca block done; scheduled acetaminophen, low-dose IV morphine for severe pain, oral oxycodone for moderate pain; avoid NSAIDs.
- Skin traction for comfort; neurovascular checks every 4 hours; bed rest, non-weight bearing.
- NPO after midnight; intramedullary nail fixation planned about 0800 tomorrow; type and screen, INR, ECG done.
- Hold anticoagulants; document last dose; SCDs and pre-operative heparin SQ for VTE prevention.
- Gentle IV fluids; delirium prevention bundle; PT/OT after surgery.

**Type 2 diabetes mellitus**
- Basal glargine with ACHS correction lispro; goal glucose 140-180 mg/dL.
- Metformin held while inpatient.
- Hypoglycemia protocol in place.

**Hypertension**
- Continue home antihypertensive; BP goal below 140/90.

**Coronary artery disease**
- Continue aspirin, statin and beta blocker; telemetry not required unless chest pain; call for chest pain or ECG changes.

**Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction**
- Euvolemic to mildly dry on exam; continue beta blocker; judicious IV fluids with daily weights.
- Continue home diuretic.

**Atrial fibrillation**
- Rate controlled on metoprolol/carvedilol.
- Apixaban held peri-operatively; resume per surgery (typically 24-48 h post-op) with DVT prophylaxis meanwhile.

**Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease**
- Scheduled DuoNebs q6h with PRN albuterol; maintenance inhaler continued.
- Oxygen goal SpO2 88-92%; avoid over-oxygenation.
- Tobacco cessation counseling and nicotine replacement.

**Chronic anemia**
- Baseline Hgb about 10; transfuse only for Hgb below 7 (or symptomatic); trend CBC.

**Gastroesophageal reflux disease**
- Continue pantoprazole (IV while NPO).

**Depression / anxiety**
- Continue sertraline; screen for suicidal ideation per policy.

**Chronic constipation**
- Continue daily regimen (hold for loose stools); opioids and immobility make it worse: add or increase laxatives early.
- Check for fecal impaction if no BM in 3 days or overflow diarrhea.

**Peripheral neuropathy**
- Continue neuropathic agent (renally dose); sedation risk if combined with opioids.
- Foot checks every shift; falls precautions.

**History of MRSA infection / colonization**
- Contact precautions; decolonization protocol (mupirocin x5 days, chlorhexidine baths).
- Include MRSA coverage in empiric antibiotics for new infection; trough/AUC monitoring if vancomycin is used.

**Rheumatoid arthritis**
- Methotrexate (WEEKLY) held during acute illness; resume only when the provider confirms infection/AKI resolved.
- Continue folic acid, hydroxychloroquine and prednisone (do not stop steroid abruptly; stress-dose if septic/hypotensive).
- Immunosuppression precautions; monitor CBC and creatinine.
- Avoid NSAIDs if CKD or anticoagulated.

**Chronic peripheral edema**
- Elevation and skin care every shift; daily weight.
- Report weeping, blisters, redness or sudden one-sided swelling (DVT/cellulitis).

**Frailty**
- Early mobility, nutrition support, delirium and fall precautions.
- Start low, go slow with medications; goals-of-care discussion.

**Prophylaxis / code status**
- DVT prophylaxis per orders; fall precautions.
- Code status: Full Code.

notes.title: Fascia iliaca compartment nerve block
notes.author: J. Whitaker, MD
notes.summary: Ultrasound-guided fascia iliaca nerve block, right hip
notes.body:
**Procedure**
- Fascia iliaca compartment nerve block

**Indication**
- Hip fracture analgesia (opioid sparing)

**Findings / technique**
Ultrasound-guided fascia iliaca block with 30 mL of ropivacaine 0.2% (below maximum dose for weight) injected deep to the fascia iliaca; good spread seen. Pain improved from 9/10 to 3/10 within 20 minutes. No paresthesia or vascular puncture. Expect 8-12 hours of relief; monitor for quadriceps weakness.

**Complications**
- None apparent. Patient tolerated the procedure; post-procedure vitals stable.
